subject: Re: MAP: Technical Evaluation Plan — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T14:12:00Z
Subject: MAP draft + Technical eval milestone (post-call)

Hi Jordan / Laura —

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to understand Acme’s priority use cases and timing. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with the technical evaluation milestone scoped out. Key items I wanted to pull forward from the call:

- Goal: Validate that Redwood can meet Acme’s latency and cost targets for the customer support triage pipeline and match or exceed baseline generation quality.
- Target close date for the MAP: 2027-01-28 (open to adjustment based on procurement timing).
- Owners: Acme tech lead (Jordan) to provide test prompts, dataset slice, and access to a performance testing environment; Redwood (Marissa/Ben) to run benchmarks, provide model shortlist and tuning suggestions.

Technical evaluation milestone (summary):
- Success criteria (benchmarks):
  - Generation quality: >90% intent-correctness on 500-sample labeled eval (binary pass/fail per example) AND acceptable human-rated quality >= 4/5 across 100 blind samples.
  - Latency: 95th percentile tail latency <= 200ms for 512-token prompt on dedicated instance profile; 50ms median target for small prompts (<=64 tokens).
  - Cost: per-1k-token inference cost benchmarked against your current baseline (please share current cost or unit of comparison). Target is <= 0.6x current cost while meeting quality/latency targets.
- Model shortlist to evaluate (initial): [Llama 2 70B (quantized), Mistral-Instant-34B, RedPajama-INCITE-70B (fine-tune candidate)]
- Evaluation deliverables: benchmark report (latency, cost, quality), sample transcripts, recommended configuration (batching, KV cache, quantization), and a short playbook for rolling to Dedicated if results are positive.
- Dependencies: 
  - Acme to provide test corpus and representative traffic profile by 2026-12-09.
  - Procurement checklist / SOC2 evidence requested (I attached a checklist of items we typically need).

Attachments: ACME-MAP-DRAFT-v1.pdf (MAP draft), acme-technical-eval-template.xlsx (benchmark template).

Proposed next steps:
1) Jordan: confirm you can deliver the 600-sample labeled eval + traffic profile by 2026-12-09.
2) Ben (SE): tentatively schedule benchmark window 2026-12-12 -> 2026-12-16.
3) Marissa/Camila: finalize model shortlist and test harness.

If that timeline works, I’ll lock it in and send a calendar invite for the kickoff.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Subject: Re: MAP draft + Technical eval milestone (post-call)

Thanks Marissa — this looks comprehensive and aligned to what we discussed. A few clarifying questions:

1) On the 500-sample labeled eval: we have an internal set of 1,200 past tickets; can we provide a 600-sample slice instead (to keep a small holdout)?
2) The latency numbers look great — can you confirm whether the 95th <=200ms target assumes a Dedicated pool (reserved GPU) or is that for hosted shared capacity?
3) For cost comparison: our current baseline is approx $1.60 / 1k tokens for our existing vendor; target cost <= $1.00 / 1k tokens would be ideal.

One more ask: loop in our procurement contact (Laura) for the SOC2 checklist so she can start reviewing the documents. Also copying our platform engineer, Raj Patel (raj.patel@acme.com), who will run the local integration tests.

Jordan
Senior Engineering Manager, Acme Corp
jordan.miller@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acme.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Smith <laura.smith@acme.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP draft + Technical eval milestone (post-call)

Jordan — great, thanks for the quick responses and for adding Raj/Laura. Answers inline below and updated asks: 

1) 600-sample slice is fine — the important part is a held-out test set (~20%) for final verification. Please include labels for the 600 sample set or indicate if you want Redwood to label a blind set (we can do that as a professional services add-on).

2) The 95th <=200ms target assumes Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) configured with our low-latency instance profile. On hosted/shared capacity we typically see higher 95th latencies during peak; we’ll include both hosted vs dedicated runs in the benchmark report so you can compare.

3) Understood on cost baseline — thank you for the number. We’ll target <= $1.00 / 1k tokens where feasible while hitting quality/latency. We’ll include a cost sensitivity table in the deliverable.

Updated responsibilities / timeline:
- Acme (Jordan/Raj): deliver 600-sample labeled eval + representative traffic profile by 2026-12-09.
- Procurement (Laura): initial review of SOC2 checklist by 2026-12-10.
- Redwood (Marissa/Ben): schedule benchmark runs 2026-12-12 -> 2026-12-16; deliver benchmark report by 2026-12-20.
- Target MAP close: 2027-01-28 (dependent on procurement/contract timeline).

Ben — can your team run the Dedicated-profile benchmarks during the 12-16 window and capture sample transcripts + cost calc? I’ll create the kickoff invite.

Thanks,
Marissa
